      - @2.01s, 1% down: "This example showcases a collection of useful temporal patterns and behaviours / that can be implemented with ossia score's temporal semantics"

      - @2.06s, 53% down: "When you hit play, things have to be connected / to the beginning of the document, in some way, / otherwise nothing will start automatically."
      - @2.07s, 35% down: "3. An interval: the long blue / line. / An interval always connects / states. / This is what contains / processes, effects, curves, / etc. / Note that the interval / is the root element of the / score timeline."
      - @7.04s, 39% down: "5. A condition. / This can be applied to an event, / to implement if-then-else, / pattern-matching or / switch-case behaviours. / To create one on a state, select it / and press C or the button in the / inspector to the right."
      - @7.07s, 29% down: "Without anything else, this doesn't / have any execution difference with the / event created before, the difference will / come after."
      - @7.08s, 19% down: "From any state you can / add another state on the same / time sync by selecting it, keeping / Alt / Option pressed, / and dragging the little / yellow cross that appears / on top-right."
      - @7.08s, 12% down: "4. A time sync. / Time syncs connect / multiple events / (and thus multiple / states)."
      - @12.11s, 38% down: "To create a state with / a trigger, simply double-click / in the background of the score. / Now, when you hit play it becomes / yellow : it indicates it can be triggered, / by clicking on the trigger button. / By default, floating trigger like this / one operate in an on-off manner: / - pressing the trigger triggers it / - pressing again cancels it / - pressing again re-triggers it / The auto-trigger mode in the inspector / instead re-arms the trigger as soon as / it executed, which works better for / instance for making drum machines, etc."
      - @12.13s, 12% down: "6. Conditions span an event, / not a complete time sync: / in the following structure, / all the conditions will be evaluated / simultaneously. / The states without condition / will always execute. / The others will only execute / if their condition evaluates to true / at this point in time."
      - @12.14s, 33% down: "7. Triggers are used to / trigger elements of the / timeline interactively."
      - @17.99s, 10% down: "8. A trigger will start / all the events and states / of a time sync at the same / time, in a synchronous and / exact fashion - all event triggering / inside the score is sample-accurate / and synchronous in the / "synchronous programming" / sense, two states on the same / time sync will never execute / at a different frame."
      - @18.07s, 38% down: "9. Time syncs stop what's before / them when they execute"
      - @24.11s, 8% down: "10. Intervals can have min and max / bounds. / Triggering messages before active / intervals are in their min bounds / are ignored"
      - @30.95s, 8% down: "11. False conditions remove their / following branches from the execution / graph."
